title: Daily News Quiz · 2026-09-10
headline: Injectable hydrogel from University at Buffalo could keep arthritis drugs working for weeks

questions.prompt: Who developed the injectable hydrogel for osteoarthritis?
choices: Scientists at the University at Buffalo
questions.hintKo: The hydrogel team is at the University at Buffalo.

questions.prompt: What happens to the hydrogel after it is injected into a joint?
choices: It becomes a semisolid depot that releases drugs for weeks
questions.hintKo: The gel firms up inside the joint and slowly releases drugs.

questions.prompt: When might patients benefit from fewer injections if this works?
choices: After clinical trials show the depot lasts weeks in the joint
When sardine sales jump thirty percent
At the moment a rocket reaches orbit
questions.hintKo: Fewer injections would follow successful clinical use, not ancient history.

questions.prompt: Where does the hydrogel aim to keep medicine concentrated?
choices: Inside the arthritic joint rather than spreading through the body
questions.hintKo: The design targets the joint space, not outer space or mines.

questions.prompt: Why do current arthritis injections often fail patients long term?
choices: Their effects are short-lived and drugs wash out of joint fluid quickly
Dark matter flashes hide the drugs
questions.hintKo: Current shots wear off because drugs leave the joint too fast.

questions.prompt: How does the gel release its medicine over time?
choices: Through diffusion and gradual relaxation of the matrix over weeks
questions.hintKo: Release is gradual through the gel matrix, not through rockets or banking.
